newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on crop weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on crop weather concerns.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher on fears of possible weather damage to U.S. and Argentine wheat, traders said.
Traders said new crop values were buoyed by forecasts for bitter cold temperatures and no snow cover this week in the central and southern U.S. Plains.

Old crop values, meanwhile, were supported by prospects of recent weather damage to Argentine wheat. Analysts on Monday were trying to calculate how much of Argentina's crop may have to be sold as feed wheat as a result of damage caused by severe storms last week in the southern part of the country.
"I think basically what you saw today was people revisiting their supply and demand tables for the current year and maybe realizing that end stocks will be tighter than expected," a KCBT trader said.

Crop concerns allowed the market to shrug off Farmland's delivery of 250,000 bushels of wheat against the KCBT Dec contract. Further bullish sentiment came from talk that Russia may be offered credit to buy 200,000 tonnes of wheat.
KCBT wheat closed 3-3/4 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 5-1/2 cents at $4.48. March was up 3-3/4 cents at $4.08-1/2.
Traders said Wolcott Lincoln sold 1.1 million July and Prudential bought 1.5 million July. CIS bought one million March and sold 1.3 million May. Prudential bought 1.5 million July, they said.
